title: Switching from Vanilla JS to React once the project is almost finished ?
author: Voiston44
selftext:
Hello everyone, I'm currently working on a browser-based Pokémon idle game and I've made good progress. Everything is functional, but here's the problem: This was my first project, and I'm using vanilla JavaScript. The project is starting to get quite large for me (around 120,000 lines of code spread across about a hundred files).



Is switching to React really advisable in my case? The AI ​​will be handling 95% of the work. Besides Opus and GPT-5.5, what model can perform this kind of task without too many errors? Will I gain much in terms of code maintenance and development ease?

comments.author: Former_Produce1721
comments.body:
React will make it harder to maintain as it's built for really complex applications with large teams

Angular or Svelte would be better

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body: Can you explain in a little more detail why you would make those choices?

replies.author: MeasIIDX
replies.body:
I think a good idea would be to look at the introduction documentation for React, Vue, Angular and Svelte and try to see which one *feels* good to you in regards to understand what's going on. You can also ask AI as well to compare them for vibe coders.

Otherwise, if you have a lot of dynamic elements in your game I'd personally recommend a JavaScript library like one of the above. Something like Vue and React can be as simple as you need them to be or as robust using their frameworks like Next or Nuxt for more complex applications.

Why a lot of people vibe with react is that the LLMs understand it very well due to it very popular so there's a lots of knowledge to pull from.

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body:
After some research I have the impression that the best Implementation Complexity / LLM Performance / Performance ratio for my game is Vue. If I understood correctly React is very well managed by LLMs but can worsen my performance if poorly used with a lot of dynamic elements. For Svelte, apparently the LLMs would be a little less effective.

I think I'll dig deeper for TypeScript + Vite+ Vue.

replies.author: MeasIIDX
replies.body:
I'm using Vue (and Nuxt) for my web game as well and it's working very well with 30 player PvP using web sockets.

I also gravitate towards Vue because it's what I mainly use at work since 2015 so maybe I'm a bit biased 😂.

replies.author: MeasIIDX
replies.body:
Personally I use Vue with my projects. I can see Angualr's split approach for components instead of SPCs like Vue helpful for agents to parse through (at least it was split when I was using it 5 years ago).

For a vibe coder trying to understand the code itself, I feel like Vue offers good readability. I never enjoyed working with JSX haha.

comments.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
comments.body: Do you need a framework for this? In my experience just pure ts client with vite for hmr works better for games.

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body:
I'm not exactly sure what I need. In any case, I have a lot of data to display, sprites, progress bars that need frequent updates, etc., and right now, performance is pretty poor. My Layout, Layerize, and Parse HTML processes account for 50% of the total time; out of 15 seconds, I have almost 5 seconds of rendering time—that's absolutely enormous, isn't it?

That's why I was thinking about React.

replies.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
replies.body:
have you made an effort to optimize what you have? 

react isn't really designed for games where state is constantly changing, it is very possible you spend time moving your stuff to react and it is just as slow if not worse. 

however, regardless of what you use, react, vanilla js, ts, etc. your performance potential is more or less the same - you just end up fighting different battles. 

I'd spend a few days trying to fix the biggest bottlenecks and seeing how much improvement is possible.

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body:
I've done quite a bit, yes, but it's probably far from enough. I still have PNG images, and my \`document.getElementsByTagName('\*').length\` command returns a number between 7500 and 10500...

So, would it be best to switch to TypeScript to facilitate maintenance and optimize what I already have without a framework?

replies.author: Free_Afternoon_7349
replies.body:
ts will forsure make it easier for the AI to work on your project and prevent a few classes of bugs 

but switching 120k lines to anything is going to be a decent chunk of work so maybe it is better to finish the project, do whatever you plan to do with it, and then if it is successful and you plan to work on it for years to engage in such

when you ask the AI to analyze your codebase and help you find performance issues what does it flag?

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body: The AI ​​tells me that my biggest gains would be image optimization, refactoring my updateDisplay and migrating to ES modules, I did everything else.

comments.author: florodude
comments.body: Coding a Pokemon game in vanilla js is why you hear us say on hear that it's worth it to spend time learning architecture

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body:
Why learning architecture when you can just burn million of token for switching after some months ? 

![gif](giphy|jOpLbiGmHR9S0)

comments.author: InterestingFrame1982
comments.body: I mean, I love writing in Vanilla JS - almost more than anything else.  If it's working, and you are enjoying it, keep on plugging.  React will always be an easy transition for someone who has a deep understanding of the language it is built on.

replies.author: Voiston44
replies.body:
I like it, and (normally) everything works; the code is easier for a beginner to understand at first. 

But imagine a first project, made with AI, 120,000 lines long, with a Pokémon theme, adding a prestige system, several game modes, quest, etc... that's probably a lot of spaghettis !

 Performance-wise, it's not really noticeable on PC because we have now good specs, but on a smartphone, for example, the game was so power-hungry that I had to add an option to disable all visual effects. And debugging or checking that the damage formulas, etc., are correct isn't easy; I often have to play to test things, and it gets tedious, even though I love playing it! 😅
